versions.short: The bill would direct the Secretary of State, working with the Secretary of Energy, to promote geothermal energy abroad to support United States interests, especially in the Indo-Pacific region. It would require a report within 180 days assessing global geothermal resources and the countries where development would most benefit U.S. security and economic interests, including whether foreign countries of concern are involved in those sectors. It would require the creation of an International Geothermal Program within one year, including public-private partnerships for exploring and developing geothermal and next-generation geothermal systems. It would require selecting at least five partner countries, including at least three in the Indo-Pacific, and pursuing agreements with them. It would also set up an advisory group of U.S. geothermal developers, manufacturers, financial institutions, and nonprofits, and require a strategy report and annual reports to Congress on the program's activities and assistance. The bill would further authorize the government to coordinate grants, loans, loan guarantees, and other financial assistance to partner countries and U.S. companies working through the program.
